_note: Shared fallback questions. A job's own bank is topped up from here, preferring questions whose tags match keywords found in that job description.

questions.text: Walk me through your background and what brought you here.
Tell me about yourself in ninety seconds.
Why this role, and why now?
What do you know about what we do, and what made you apply?
What are you looking for in your next role that you don't have today?
Walk me through the project you're proudest of. What was your specific contribution?
Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate. How did it resolve?
Describe a time you disagreed with your manager's decision.
Tell me about a project that failed. What did you actually learn?
Describe a time you shipped something you weren't proud of. Why did you ship it?
Tell me about a time you had to say no to a stakeholder.
Describe a situation where the requirements were completely unclear. What did you do first?
Tell me about a time you changed your mind based on new information.
When have you gone beyond what was asked of you, and was it worth it?
Tell me about the hardest bug you've ever debugged.
Describe a time you had to make a technical decision with incomplete information.
Tell me about a piece of technical debt you chose to live with. What was the reasoning?
How do you decide when a system needs to be rewritten versus refactored?
Walk me through how you'd design a system to handle a hundred times your current traffic.
How do you approach making something slow become fast? Walk me through a real example.
What does good test coverage mean to you in practice, not in theory?
Tell me about a time you caused a production incident. What happened next?
How do you decide what to build first when everything seems urgent?
Your project is going to miss its deadline by two weeks. Walk me through exactly what you do.
You inherit a codebase nobody understands and a feature is due Friday. What's your first day look like?
A teammate keeps shipping work that needs rework. How do you handle it?
How would you spend your first thirty days in this role?
Tell me about a time you mentored someone. What changed for them?
How do you give critical feedback to someone more senior than you?
Describe a time you led without formal authority.
Tell me about a decision you made that you'd reverse today.
How do you keep a team aligned when people disagree on direction?
Tell me about a metric you moved. How did you know it was actually you?
Describe a time the data contradicted what everyone believed.
How do you decide whether a result is real or noise?
Walk me through an experiment you designed end to end.
Tell me about a time you had to explain something technical to a non-technical audience.
Describe the hardest customer conversation you've had.
How do you find out what a customer actually needs versus what they asked for?
Tell me about a time you pushed back on a product requirement.
How do you handle a user-facing bug that only affects one important customer?
What's the trade-off you make most often in frontend work?
How do you think about component boundaries in a large frontend codebase?
Tell me how you'd debug a page that feels slow but profiles clean.
How do you approach accessibility when nobody is asking for it?
Walk me through how you'd design an API that other teams will depend on.
How do you handle a schema migration on a table that can't go down?
What's your approach to handling failure in a distributed system?
How do you evaluate whether a model is good enough to ship?
Tell me about a time a model behaved badly in production.
How do you think about the security implications of a feature you're building?
Describe the most chaotic environment you've worked in. How did you stay effective?
What breaks first when a team grows from five to fifteen people?
How do you protect focus time when everything is an interrupt?
What's something you believe about building software that most people disagree with?
What's the biggest gap in your skills right now, and what are you doing about it?
How do you learn something genuinely new? Walk me through the last time.
What kind of work makes you lose track of time?
Why are you leaving your current role?
What questions do you have for me?
Is there anything you wish I'd asked you?
